mainTopic: The end of פרק הישן (sins that cause wealth to be lost, and the praise of the humble), then the opening משנה of פרק לולב הגזול and the גמרא's question about a stolen לולב after the first day.
overview: This amud finishes פרק הישן and opens a new chapter. First, the גמרא ends a list of sins that make people lose their property to the government, such as failing to protest wrongdoing and breaking public צדקה pledges. רב then gives his own list of four sins: delaying a worker's pay, withholding it, pushing communal burdens onto others, and גסות הרוח. He says arrogance is as bad as all the others together, and he closes with a פסוק promising the humble the land and peace. After the הדרן, פרק לולב הגזול begins with a משנה that sorts each kind of לולב into פסול or כשר. A stolen, dry, אשירה, or עיר הנדחת לולב is פסול, and so is one whose top or leaves were cut off. A לולב with spread leaves, one from the palms of הר הברזל, and one three טפחים long are כשר. The גמרא then asks why a stolen לולב is פסול after the first day, since ״לָכֶם״ seems to apply only to day one. It begins an answer from רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the list: failing to protest and broken charity pledges
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list of reasons that people's property is lost to the government. The last two reasons are not protesting wrongdoing when you could, and pledging צדקה in public without paying.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of people who had the power to protest wrongdoing and did not protest, and because of people who publicly pledge charity and then do not give it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list that started just before this passage. The list gives reasons why the property of בעלי בתים is lost to the government.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These last two items are about responsibility to others. One is a person who had the power to stop sinners and stayed silent. The other is a person who promised צדקה in front of everyone and never paid. Both are failures of a promise or a duty, and the punishment is losing one's money.

keyTerms.meaning: They had the ability (the power in their hand)
To protest against, to stop someone from sinning
Pledging (committing to give) charity

phrases.english: and on account of those who had the ability in their hand
to protest, and did not protest,
and on account of those who pledge charity in public
and do not give.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל שֶׁהָיָה סִפֵּק בְּיָדָם לִמְחוֹת וְלֹא מִיחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא list that began before this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Failing to protest when you could, and not paying a public charity pledge, cause a person's property to be lost.

steps.title: רב's four sins that make wealth disappear
steps.stepSummary: רב gives his own list of four sins that make homeowners lose their property to the treasury. They are delaying a worker's pay, withholding a worker's pay, pushing communal burdens onto others, and arrogance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Because of four things, the property of homeowners is lost to the government treasury. It is lost because of those who delay a hired worker's pay, those who withhold a hired worker's pay, those who throw the communal burden off their own necks and put it on their friends, and arrogance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a second list of four sins that cause property to be lost. This parallels the ברייתא that just ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three of the four sins are about how wealthy people mistreat others with their money or power. Two are cheating workers out of their pay, by paying late or not at all. The third is avoiding one's share of community duties and leaving them to others. The fourth, גסות הרוח, is an attitude rather than an action, and the next step singles it out.

keyTerms.meaning: The government treasury; money that goes there is lost for good
Homeowners, people with property
Those who hold back (delay) a hired worker's wages
Those who withhold or cheat a worker of his wages
Throwing off a burden (avoiding responsibility)

phrases.english: Rav said:
On account of four things
the property of homeowners goes out to the government treasury:
on account of those who delay a hired worker's wages,
and on account of those who withhold a hired worker's wages,
and on account of those who throw off the yoke from their own necks
and place it on their friends,
and on account of arrogance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: בִּשְׁבִיל אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים נִכְסֵי בַּעֲלֵי בָּתִּים יוֹצְאִין לְטִמְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel list from רב, following the ברייתא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Delaying wages, withholding wages, shifting communal burdens onto others, and arrogance cause a homeowner's property to be lost.

steps.title: Arrogance outweighs all, but the humble inherit the land
steps.stepSummary: רב adds that arrogance alone weighs as much as all the other sins. In contrast, a פסוק promises the humble that they will inherit the land and enjoy peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: And arrogance is equal to all of them. But about the humble it is written: 'And the humble will inherit the land and delight in an abundance of peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב points out that arrogance, the last item on his list, is as bad as all the others put together. He then closes with a פסוק about the reward of the humble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is ranking the items. Arrogance is not just one of four; it weighs as much as the whole list. The פסוק gives the opposite picture. The arrogant lose their property, while the humble 'inherit the land,' which means they gain and keep what they have.

keyTerms.meaning: Arrogance, haughtiness
Equal to all of them together
The humble

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק ends on a message about character. Arrogance is the worst of the sins that destroy wealth, and humility brings inheritance and peace.

phrases.english: And arrogance is equal to all of them.
But about the humble it is written:
"And the humble will inherit the land
and delight themselves in an abundance of peace."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the last item of רב's list and closes with a contrasting פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Arrogance equals all the other sins combined, while the humble are promised the land and peace.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הישן
steps.stepSummary: This is the formula that closes the chapter called הישן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter הישן.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter called הישן. It does not teach a new law; it is a closing formula.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן is a custom of saying goodbye to a chapter we have learned and promising to come back to it. The chapter is called by its opening word, הישן ('one who sleeps'), from the משנה about sleeping under a bed in the סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula said when finishing a chapter
'One who sleeps', the name of the chapter just finished

phrases.english: We will return to you, "HaYashen"
phrases.notes: Each chapter is named after its first words; this one opened with הַיָּשֵׁן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after its final aggadic teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק הישן is complete; a new chapter begins next.

steps.title: A לולב that is unfit because of where it came from or its condition
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with a list of a לולב that is פסול. These are a stolen one, a dry one, one from an אשירה, and one from an עיר הנדחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A stolen לולב and a dry לולב are unfit. A לולב from an אשירה tree and one from an עיר הנדחת are unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה about which לולב can be used for the מצוה. It starts with a לולב that is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these cases are about where the לולב came from, not what it looks like. It might be stolen, or it might come from a tree worshipped as עבודה זרה or from a city condemned for idol worship. 'Dry' is the one case about its physical state. The גמרא will soon explain why each one is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The basic teaching that the גמרא then discusses
A stolen לולב; also the name of this new chapter
Dry, dried out
Unfit, cannot be used for the מצוה
A tree that is worshipped as idolatry
A city whose people were led into idol worship, and whose property must be burned

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a stolen לולב is פסול because something is wrong with the plant itself. It may look perfect. The problem is how the person got it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The case of a stolen לולב gives the chapter its name, and the גמרא will build an important discussion around it.

phrases.english: A stolen lulav and a dry one are unfit.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל אֲשֵׁירָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: One of an asheira, and one of a city led astray, is unfit.
phrases.notes: The word לולב is understood here: a לולב taken from an אֲשֵׁירָה or from an עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter with a new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לולב that is stolen, dry, from an אשירה, or from an עיר הנדחת is פסול.

steps.title: A damaged לולב: cut top and torn leaves versus spread leaves
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a לולב is פסול if its top was cut off or its leaves were torn off. It is כשר if the leaves only spread apart. רבי יהודה says one should tie the leaves together at the top.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its top was cut off, or its leaves were torn off, it is unfit. If its leaves spread apart, it is fit. רבי יהודה says: one should tie it at the top.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from where the לולב came from to physical damage to the לולב. It separates damage that makes it פסול from damage that does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cut-off top or leaves torn away count as real damage, so the לולב is פסול. If the leaves are still attached but have spread away from the spine, the לולב is still כשר. רבי יהודה adds that in that case you should tie the leaves back together at the top.

keyTerms.meaning: Its top was cut off
Its leaves were torn off
Its leaves spread apart (but are still attached)
Fit, can be used for the מצוה
He should tie it (bind it together)

steps.confusionAlert: נִפְרְצוּ and נִפְרְדוּ sound almost the same but are opposite rulings. נִפְרְצוּ means torn off, so it is פסול. נִפְרְדוּ means only spread apart, so it is כשר.

phrases.english: If its top was cut off,
or if its leaves were torn off, it is unfit.
If its leaves spread apart, it is fit.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
One should tie it from the top.
phrases.notes: He is talking about the last case: tie the spread-out leaves back against the spine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from the source of the לולב to its physical damage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cut top or torn-off leaves make a לולב פסול; leaves that only spread apart leave it כשר, and רבי יהודה says to tie them at the top.

steps.title: Palms of הר הברזל and the minimum length of a לולב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a לולב from the palms of הר הברזל is כשר. A לולב that is three טפחים long, enough to shake, is also כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Palms of הר הברזל are fit. A לולב that is three טפחים long, enough to shake it, is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends this section with two more cases of a לולב that is כשר. One is an unusual kind of palm, and the other sets the minimum size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Palms from הר הברזל look different from normal ones; their leaves are shorter and do not cover the whole spine. Even so, they are כשר. The משנה then gives a minimum size: three טפחים, which is long enough to do the shaking that the מצוה requires.

keyTerms.meaning: Palms from the 'Iron Mountain', an unusual type of palm
Handbreadths, a unit of measure
To shake (wave) the לולב

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה sorts each לולב into פסול or כשר. A לולב is פסול if it comes from a forbidden source or is badly damaged. It is still כשר if the leaves have only spread, if it is an unusual palm of הר הברזל, or if it is at least three טפחים long so it can be shaken.

phrases.english: Palms of the Iron Mountain are fit.
A lulav that has in it three handbreadths
enough to shake with it, is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with more cases of a לולב that is כשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Palms of הר הברזל are כשר, and a לולב of three טפחים, long enough to shake, is כשר.

steps.title: The משנה's ruling on a stolen לולב has no time limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא observes that the משנה states its rule without any limits. A stolen לולב is פסול on the first day and on the later days alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה states its ruling without any qualification. There is no difference between the first day of יום טוב and the second day of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out that the משנה made no distinction between days. It says a stolen לולב is פסול on day one and on day two alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה simply said "a stolen לולב is פסול" and did not say "only on the first day." The גמרא reads this as a blanket rule. This sets up the question that comes next: why should the later days follow the same strict rule?

keyTerms.meaning: It states the rule flatly, with no exceptions
There is no difference
The first day of the festival
Stolen

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It teaches the rule without qualification,
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה, which listed a stolen לולב as פסול without mentioning any particular day.

phrases.english: there is no difference whether on the first day of the festival,
and no difference whether on the second day of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's first case, the stolen לולב listed in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the plain wording of the משנה, a stolen לולב is פסול on every day of סוכות, not only the first.

steps.title: Why would a stolen לולב be unfit after the first day?
steps.stepSummary: A dry לולב is פסול every day because it lacks beauty. A stolen one is clearly פסול on the first day because of ״לָכֶם״. But why should it be פסול on the later days?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a dry one: we need "beauty" (הָדָר), and a dry one does not have it. But a stolen one only makes sense on the first day, since it is written ״לָכֶם״, meaning "from your own." On the second day, why should it not work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the blanket rule from Step 8. The reason a dry לולב is פסול applies every day, but the reason a stolen one is פסול seems tied only to the first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with a dry לולב is that it is missing הָדָר, and that applies on every day. The problem with a stolen לולב comes from the word ״לָכֶם״ in the פסוק about "the first day," so it should only apply to day one, when the obligation is from the Torah. On the later days, which are a rabbinic practice, that source does not seem to apply. So why does the משנה make it פסול then too?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (introduces the easy case before the hard one)
Beauty; the four species must be beautiful
From your own property
Why?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not doubting that a stolen לולב is פסול on the first day. That part is clear from ״לָכֶם״. The only question is about the later days.

phrases.english: It makes sense for a dry one —
we require "beauty," and it is not there.
phrases.notes: The word "beauty" comes from ויקרא 23:40, the same פסוק about taking the four species.

phrases.english: But a stolen one,
it makes sense on the first day of the festival,
as it is written: "for yourselves" — from your own.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי אַמַּאי לָא?
phrases.english: But on the second day of the festival, why not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the blanket rule that Step 8 read out of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a stolen לולב is פסול even on the days after the first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source for disqualifying a stolen לולב (״לָכֶם״) is tied to the first day, so on the later days there seems to be no reason to disqualify it.

steps.title: The answer begins in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces its answer through רבי יוחנן quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי. The content of the answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the answer to the question in Step 9. It only tells us who is answering, and the actual answer comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why a stolen לולב is פסול after the first day. The גמרא now brings a teaching that רבי יוחנן passed on from רבי שמעון בן יוחי, which will explain this. Keep the question in mind, because the next lines give the reason.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the answer to the challenge raised in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Answer introduced by a quoted teaching; its content follows in the continuation of the text.
